review: A creatively imagined multiplayer game. A surprisingly pleasant alternative to the brawler-type of multiplayer that has become so commonplace (e.g. samurai gunn, starwal, towerfall, bit-brawlers, brawlhalla, etc...), SpeedRunners offers players a spectrum of depth in gameplay. At its base, this game is a racing platformer, rewarding players who learn the turns and obstacles of various unique levels while punishing those who make mistakes. Perfectionism at its finest. This fine work does offer a deeper level of competition, however, if players chooses to exploit the nuances of the game's physics. With the mention of the glory of this game, I must also point out the negatives, which are frustratingly apparent within the first 5 minutes of gameplay. The matchmaking system is extremely unreliable, despite the implementation of a ranking system (albeit new). There are constant bugs in just about any multiplayer game, which would be endurable in a more forgiving game. The glitches can be brutal, and, due to the competitive nature of this game, they do not come off as humorous as in other games. At the rate at which this game has improved recently and with the massive community of stakeholders which it has garnered, SpeedRunners, while still in Beta at the moment of this review, will doubtlessly become one of the flawless go-to's for just about any friendly LAN party and competitive tournament. Each complaint I have for this game is tied to a problem that any early access game would have, and they are no reason to avoid a purchase. Currently an 8 / 10, this game is an easy pick-up and a difficult put-down!

Speedrunners, a game of reflexes and grapple hooking your friends.

You really should get this game, honestly. It's definitely worth the friend rage. Also, the only issue I have right now would be the blast zone lines aren't transparent, which they should REALLY do. 

Analysis:

Speedrunners is a game of running around a big map, grapple hooking your way to first place. Of course, it's only possible to grapple white ceilings, so the majority (unless allowed) of the map is going to be running, picking up item boxes, and trying to get to first place. What you have to do is make sure you keep on running til you can't. By that time you've hopefully won your first round. The game is in Early Access right now, but it's getting a lot better! The controls are also configurable and it's really best with a controller.

The items while not that plentiful are actually really fun regardless. You have rockets to shoot at people, EMP blasts to destroy: grapples, golden grapples, boxes, and also rockets; invincibility shield drill which protects you from harm, golden grapples which hook onto the closest player in the direction you face, and 3 boxes.

Speedrunners also has a nice twist to it where you can choose different modes to play. The most frustratingly fun has to be the mirrored track mode. Rapture just shoots rockets everywhere, lethal spikes, all X (X being either rockets or golden grapples last time I checked), and there may or may not be another I'm forgetting at the moment, but that's the fun of this game.

tl;dr Speedrunners is a REALLY fun friend rage-inducing game that makes you want to keep trying to aim for the top, but also can be played casually enough for fun.

[h1]The game.[/h1]
[i]SpeedRunners[/i] is a multiplayer running game where 4 players fight against each other. In fact, SR is a cross between a platformer and a racing game. You can run, jump, swing around, and use devious weapons and pick-ups to knock opponents off-screen.

[h1]Gameplay.[/h1]
This game is good, fun and challenging. Has very simple controls and its super easy to play. But you need patience to practice and hone all your MLG skills in order to win. Although 4 player Coop would require you to have 4 controllers (3 with a keyboard) on a PC. You'll always be racing against three others characters in the story mode, but in the multiplayer you can customise the matches to race against one, two or three other people, whether that is local or online. A player has to win 3 times before they win the round. [i]Speedrunners[/i] is that kind of game that makes you really entertained because of it's fast-thinking way.

If the race begins to take too long, the actual screen itself will start getting smaller and smaller, making it easier to drop out. Dropping out of the screen and dying is not a new concept in games, but the way it is done in [i]SpeedRunners[/i] feels quite different from anything else because of the pure speed and traversal mechanics used to keep you running, and alive. But there are other times when your opponent is totally off screen and yet they don't die. Consistency is definitely not applied across the board. Sometimes it's too frustrating and can become a issue of the game.

I like a deep singleplayer story mode and what SR presents is a bit short and defective. The AI can be a bit robotic and uninteresting and the hard mode is made for masochists. All the leveling up and XP earned just unlocks multiplayer perks like levels, characters and skins. So there isn't much motivation there for me to re-play and continue to rack up the XP beyond one hard mode playthrough. For the hardcore achievement hunters out there all that I can say is: good luck. This game has a ridiculously few hardcore ones that will take many hours of playing, and a few weapon ones that are pure luck based.

Graphically is nice just like the skins that are diverse and fun. The only problem is the ranking mode, where you can try and will probably fail to get an online ranking match unless you wait at least 5 minutes if you're lucky. Besides that, it's a good game and of course, it will be a better game if you have friends to play with. Playing this game alone is good, but not for too many time, at least for me. It's a relatively competitive indie game on the market.

Speedrunners: Gotta go fast

Do you like racing games like Mario Kart, 1950’s esque artwork, superheroes, well designed video games, and having fun? Well, my friend, then SpeedRunners is for you!

Because it’s all of those things wrapped into one really well made package.

SpeedRunners is a racing game, first and foremost. The setup being that various superheroes are racing to the scene of a crime, or emergency, and trying to beat each other there! At least that’s what I got out of it, the game is light on story; but it honestly doesn’t need it, the gameplay is what shines here. And boy, let me tell you, it really shines. This game is polished. It’s incredibly smooth, responsive, and just feels good. Like peeling the plastic off of a new cellphone.

And surprisingly, SpeedRunners is an Early Access game! It’s still in Beta! I continuously find myself being shocked at just how good this game handles. It feels like a full fledged release, and I give the developers, DoubleDutch Games, credit because SpeedRunners is fantastic. This is in part because of the wonderful ‘track’ designs present here. A good racing game is crippled if it doesn’t have fun courses, which SpeedRunners delivers on. There are twelve or so levels, and only two that I dislike. That’s a pretty successful margin.

Now, unlike any other racing game I have played, SpeedRunners involves… running! Who would have thought, right?

And despite being a foot race, SpeedRunners maintains an excellent sense of speed. Four players all running at breakneck speeds trying to usurp each other. Throwing missiles, freeze-rays, hooks, and crates left and right hoping to trip each other up. The highs are high, and the lows are looooow. Being in first place, getting hit by a missile, tumbling around and ending up in last place-- and then dead-- is jarring. You’ll get mad at your friends. But when you do it, it’s oh so sweet.

Each race is an elimination race where each ‘lap’ continues on until only one runner remains. Other players are eliminated by advancing far enough ahead that the edge of the screen touches someone. Then they explode, are out of the race, and the screen’s border progressively closes in until it’s just a tiny rectangle big enough for two players. This requires you to memorize the tracks very well, because at that point you’re almost literally playing blind.

It gets real intense real fast.

As with most multiplayer games, SpeedRunners is best with friends. But the game also offers some really, really, good bots that actually offer a decent challenge. And it has a very active multiplayer! I’ve never not found a game, which is great… Although I have occasionally run into some particularly douche-y people… But it is the internet so that’s to be expected.

I beat another player using the hook, this game’s equivalent of the ‘blue shell’, and he promptly told me in all caps to leave the game and engage in sexual congress with myself. I called him out on this, and he told me I was being rude for using the item. I proceeded to handle this situation quite poorly. But that’s another story!

Internet antics aside, SpeedRunners is fantastic and certainly one of my favorite games of 2015. Even if it came out in 2013. 2013’s 2015 racing game of the year.

SpeedRunners is just a joy to play. Even alone. And for $15 it’s a total steal. There is tons of content in this game, with like a billion different Runners and like ten skins for each one. They also have workshop support so that the community can create levels… Sadly I have only played a few workshop levels that even come close to the amazing quality of the developer courses.

I will wholeheartedly recommend SpeedRunners to anyone looking for a cool local co-op game. Or, hell, anyone looking for a competitive racing game.

It’s that good.

Seriously, go buy it. These guys deserve the support.

Speedrunners is a fast-paced, competitive, racing game where players play as superheroes trying to outrun each other in 16 different official maps, in addition to thousands of user created levels. Speedrunners offers both online and local matches that can hold up to 4 players and different game modes that suits a wide range of skill levels, from practice mode for beginners and ranked mode for more experienced players. There is also a friendly tutorial for those who are new to the game, and all these game modes are designed to suit players as they improve. As there are only 16 official maps, Speedrunners has allowed us to use our creativity to submit workshop levels, which keeps the game interesting. Although I have been held back due to connectivity problems, I have enjoyed the challenges that the game offered me regardless.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The objective of the game is to outrun each other so that one player might fall off-screen and lose. In Speedrunners players race and outwit each other through a variety of obstacles, such as crates, lasers, and spikes, and power-ups, such as fireballs, ice rays, missiles, and grappling hooks, which has often caused close wins, amazing moments, and huge upsets. Additionally, the players can adjust the settings so that the game turns a whole new turn, with mechanics such as a “Lethal Spikes”, which causes players to drop as soon as they hit a spike, and srennurdeepS, which causes the map to be flipped. However, theses additions get boring after a while, and I recommend that, in the future, the developers could add more or change features and power-ups to shift the flow of the game.

[h1]Graphics and Artwork[/h1]
In a universe where superheroes race each other to save people or capture criminals, the game design blends into this universe by using a cartoonish yet straightforward and sharp design. The variety of characters, the power-ups the players use, and the clear sound effects of explosions and ice beams all emphasize the theme of world.

[h1]Soundtrack[/h1]
I cannot lie, but the game has some amazing soundtracks, which also fits with the overall superhero theme and the fast pace of the game; however, as the soundtracks are repeated often during matches, the developers could add more soundtracks to keep the game interesting.

[h1]Other Aspects[/h1]
Speedrunners features tons of unlockable Heroes; each with their own personality and character. What’s more: they also have skins! Moreover, the community is allowed to submit trails, which gives the game even customization.

The best thing is, you can play this locally with your friends! It’s a good way to get your friends to gather around and have a few (or many) matches, although I have to say, it’s quite difficult to control your character by using a controller. I tried doing this by using a PS3 controller, and it seems that it will take more time to get used to using the controller than of the keyboard. If you don’t have friends to hang out with, well, you can always pop online for a few matches with online players, train with bots, or invite your online friends to come and have a match with you.

In conclusion, Speedrunners is an innovative and friendly game that combines superheroes with racing and lets you improve at your own pace, but somewhat lacks in the aspect that could keep a game interesting. I would recommend this to everyone who enjoy fast-paced games and racing.

SpeedRunners Review: The 1,000-Hour Grind and the Veteran Wall
​I’ve put nearly 1,000 hours into SpeedRunners, and after all that time, I can say it’s a great game, but it has two very different sides—especially lately.
​The Good: Low-Spec Frenzy and Pure Addiction
​The best thing about SpeedRunners is that it’s a truly good, high-octane game. The sense of speed is incredible. One of its biggest strengths is being a low-spec game; you don't need a powerful PC for it to run like lightning, making it super accessible. It’s the kind of game you can play every single day without even realizing how much time has passed. The mix of running, jumping, using the grappling hook, and timing your items is extremely fun and keeps you hooked as you try to perfect every lap.
​The Bad: The Skill Wall and Limited Matchmaking
​However, the downside is that since the game has been out for years, the community has changed. Currently, there is a lack of new players, which has created a serious issue. You run into players who have been around for years, and the average skill level is way above what it should be.
​This makes the ranked matchmaking feel very limited. Because the player base is small, the system constantly matches you against the same people. The frustrating part is that these players often have a lower rank than they deserve. They might look like rookies based on their badge, but they actually play much better because they’ve been dedicated to the game for a long time. It’s hard to compete fairly when you’re constantly facing these veterans in disguise, making ranking up feel more like a punishment than an achievement.
​Final Verdict
​For a new player, SpeedRunners can be intimidating because of this massive skill gap. But if you're looking for a fast, fun platformer-racer that doesn't eat up your PC resources, the core gameplay is amazing. If you have the patience to learn while losing to the same "experts" over and over, there’s a lot of fun to be had.

Crime-fighting.  Its a difficult job.  In the world of "Speedrunners" its difficult for reasons you might not have considered.  What would happen in a world where Superheroes were as prolific as those with an AA in business?  Where only the hungry and competitive get to be employed for their unique anti-villain skillsets, while the rest are relegated to fry cook duty at the local deep fry eatery.

  Speedrunners casts you as a fledgling costumed vigilante desperate to break onto the scene as 'This City's #1 Hero!"  The catch?  You are not the only one.  Thus, we come to the core of the game, which is not actually fighting crime at all; rather, its a mad dash to beat your fellow would-be champions of justice to the scene of the crime, by any means necessary.

  What does this translate to?  A Mario-Kart-esque footrace across rooftops, through buildings, and any other place you could seemingly run at semi-full bore.  Players (up to 4 of them) pick their hero of choice from a multitude of excellent original characters (and YouTube personalities!), and then beat feet (and each other), picking up power ups, swinging on grappling hooks, and tripping each other as they attempt to leave their opponents in the dust.

  The action is quite simple.  Heroes run in a repeating/looping level, attempting to have their opponents leave the shared screen by being outpaced.  This is accomplished with the help of numerous tools.  Players may find themselves in possession of seeker rockets to sling at opponents, remote mines, drop-able crates, and Scorpion-esque ranged grappling devices, just to name a few of the tools available.  Players are able to double jump and wall jump, as well as deploy grappling hooks to avoid obstacles (with mechanics similar to the ninja rope from Worms Armageddon). You can even build speed by manipulating gravity and centrifugal force with well-place grapples.

  Once the first opponent is knocked out (by meeting an untimely end at the edge of the screen as the rest of the dynamic do-gooders race on), things really begin to heat up.  The music changes, and the edges of the screen shrink, giving the remaining players less and less room to maneuver.  This can continue to a point where skilled players continue their parkour punchfest in a screen roughly 1/3 the size of normal.  Last man standing wins the round; first to 3 wins takes the match.

  Sounds delightfully simple doesn't it?  And you'd be right to think so, given the initial smattering of levels from developer tinyBuild.  The game features Steam Workshop support, and the level of complexity in some of the user generated levels can really ramp up the difficulty when it comes to twitch reactions and puzzling out the fastest, most appropriate route.  The game sports competitive multiplayer, as well as local and online play.  You may play with a keyboard or controller (the latter being this authors preference).

  Having said all that, I offer you this review and endorsement with full disclosure.  Having played this game at length with people of varying skill levels, bear the following disclaimers in mind:

- There is a bit of a learning curve here, particularly in the competitive scene.  Its ok to fail, as long as its still fun, right?
- This game is in Early Access.  Its not perfect, but it is pretty darn good.
- Furniture and peripherals may be at risk during gameplay.  Specifically, gamepads and keyboards may experience stress fractures during tense matches, or become heavily moistened by an abundance of palm perspiration.  Furniture, on the other hand, may become damaged due to severe body contractions, particularly during close matches.  To elaborate, whilst racing you may experience "butt fist," a tensing ones backside that may result in loss of underwear and damage to ones gaming chair.

If I haven't scared you off with the potential dangers above, Speedrunners is a no-brainer buy.  So, what are you waiting for?  Break out your spandex, knee-high lace boots, and cape, and prepare to race..... FOR JUSTICE!!!!!!
